scale_info.basis: Re-measured 2026-10-18. The first version pinned the line at the back door's MIDDLE row (485) instead of its base (532) and had no second check. Three references now agree on one line: the back door (80-84 in; top row 344, base row 532, 188 px) gives 2.3 px/in at row 532; the rear bar stool (my assumption: about 43 in to the top of its back; base row 773, back top row 533) gives about 5.6 at row 773; the front bar stool (back top row 610, base row 868) gives about 6.2 at row 868. A line through all three leaves at most 6% error and puts the horizon at row 333 and the eye at about 83 in. That fits the picture itself: the door's top (row 344) sits at eye level when the eye is about 83 in and the door is 80-84 in. The vanishing-point search still fails here (the whirlpool paint), so the horizon comes from the references, not from lines; the stool height is my assumption.

rear bar stool, about 43 in to the back top: 5.6 at row 773

scale_info.basis: Re-measured 2026-10-18 from the tight chair cut-outs (back top to feet), all folding chairs taken as 32 in (assumed). Wide-angle, steep downward view onto a curved staircase: no usable vanishing point, so the scale is a line fitted through chair readings only. The earlier fit had the back-row reading at the wrong row (600; the back chairs actually stand at rows 773-834), which made figures at the back of the floor too big. Five back-row chairs (105-120 px, base rows 773-834) average 3.5 px/in; two middle chairs (152 and 132 px, base rows 870-872) average 4.4; two front chairs (155 and 136 px, base row 932) average 4.5; the left chair (145 px, base row 1024) gives 4.5. Foot rows are estimates (feet are hidden in places), and upright things look foreshortened from this high angle, as an upright avatar would. Stage props (mic stand, drums) were not used: the stage is raised and their real sizes are unknown.

2 front chairs 32 in: 155 and 136 px at base row 932, mean 4.5 at row 932

bar counter, round table, stage props not used (hidden base or raised)
